title: What the Golden Pheasant wears

is_this_you.pressure: You leave on foot before the argument turns, then come back later with the verdict already sewn.
is_this_you.love: You love by arrangement: the gift chosen weeks ahead, the evening laid out in order, and not one word about what it meant.
is_this_you.cost: You wait to be invited into the light, and you keep count of every year nobody asked.

opener.text: Under the Ming and Qing, a civil official of the second rank wore a golden pheasant, 錦雞 (jǐnjī), sewn on the chest and back of his robe [s8]. Only the crane ranked above it [s8]. The bird's name sounded like a word for ruling, and writers tied it to literary talent and military prowess [s8]. That badge fits you. You rule by learning, and you dress for the part.

howto: Three parts, in order of rank.

tabs.label: Your colours
tabs.intro: Fire that wants the hall. Wood that keeps its counsel.

rows.text: Leo is fixed Fire, ruled by the Sun [s1] [s3]. The Rabbit is yin Wood, elegant and alert, and slow to reveal its mind [s4] [s5]. In you the caution feeds the brilliance. You enter the hall in full colour and say very little. When you do speak, the court writes it down.
The bird's Chinese name means brocade fowl [s20]. The Rabbit's old gifts are painting, calligraphy, tailoring and cooking [s5]. Your taste is a trade, and people trust it before you explain it.

tabs.label: Your court
tabs.intro: Influence by counsel. Love by ceremony.

rows.text: The badge belonged to a civil official, not a general [s8]. You do your finest work as counsel beside the throne, as an editor or a chief of staff.
Leo takes great pride in the relationship [s2]. So you court with ceremony. The table is set before anyone arrives. Admiration given in private holds you longer than any public praise.

tabs.label: Who you dress for
tabs.intro: Three worth the robe, and one who argues with it.
tabs.love_lead: You dress for very few people. The old pairings say who has earned the full plumage.

easy.why: The Giant Otter (Aries, Dog year) is your secret friend, since Dog and Rabbit are a Six Harmonies pair, and Aries burns with Leo's Fire [s4] [s3].
The Bar-headed Goose (Sagittarius, Goat year) shares your trine of Rabbit, Goat and Pig, and Sagittarius is the third Fire sign [s4] [s3].
The Luna Moth (Libra, Goat year) is trine kin as well, and Libra's Air feeds your Fire [s4] [s3].

hard.why: The hard one is the Hoatzin: the Rooster clashes with the Rabbit, and Aquarius sits opposite Leo [s4] [s3].

story.text: Emperor Huizong painted a golden pheasant on a bending hibiscus branch [s9]. The scroll hangs in the Palace Museum, Beijing [s10]. His poem says the tall-crowned bird already holds all five virtues [s9]. The old list reads the crown as culture, 文 (wén), and the spurs as martial skill, 武 (wǔ) [s11]. Facing an enemy is courage, 勇 (yǒng) [s11]. Calling others to food is benevolence, 仁 (rén), and keeping the night watch on time is trust, 信 (xìn) [s11]. Benevolence is also the virtue of Wood, your element [s6].

closing: Wear the robe. The rank was yours before anyone sewed it on.
